item.title: California couple's garden dispute ends in court after 1955 deal involving $250 and babysitting
item.description: A California couple who bought a home in 2019 found themselves in a legal battle after their neighbour claimed ownership of a 20-by-20-foot garden they believed was theirs. The dispute centred on a 1955 agreement involving $250, babysitting services and land access rights. On Monday, a California appeals court upheld the couple's exclusive right to use the garden.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Demolition damaged Miami home in 2014; Florida court upholds woman's $240,000 insurance victory after 12 years
item.description: In Florida, Sandra Moise faced significant challenges when her home was damaged due to vibrations from nearby demolition activities. Initially, her insurance provider, Homeowners Choice, denied her claim citing policy exclusions against earth movement. After enduring a prolonged legal battle, a jury ultimately sided with her, confirming the damage's cause.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘This is the future you want?’ White House cites France riots to slam Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description: In France, recent demonstrations regarding education and living costs have spiraled into significant unrest and violence. Initially sparked by issues in educational facilities, the protests quickly broadened to encompass widespread frustration with public services. The Trump administration seizes upon these events to castigate Democrats, linking them to growing disorder in America.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Washington appeals court upholds anti-harassment order after neighbour allegedly disrupts utilities
item.description: A dispute between a couple and their neighbour escalated into serious harassment concerning driveway access and utilities. The couple claimed that their neighbour blocked the shared driveway and cut off their water supply. This pattern of interference led them to seek legal protection from the court. The Washington Court of Appeals confirmed that their claims warranted an anti-harassment order.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An animal-borne virus called Shamonda, which normally circulates in livestock, has infected and killed a human for the first time
item.description: A 61-year-old man in France has tragically lost his life to the Shamonda virus, a disease previously only observed in animals. The man, who was battling leukaemia, contracted the virus likely through a midge bite. With documented cases of infected animals in Europe and previous outbreaks in Africa and Asia, health officials are investigating how the virus spreads and its possible risks to humans.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: North Carolina city restores 27 acres of wetlands to reduce flood risks for 93 properties
item.description: Hendersonville celebrates the successful completion of the first phase of its Lower Mud Creek Floodplain Restoration Project. This significant endeavor aims to mitigate flood risks for surrounding properties, boosting community safety. Key efforts include reconnecting Mud Creek with its floodplain to enhance water quality and flood management. Financial support from various organizations has been crucial in the project's design and construction.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Henry F. Porter Preserve Deal: 181 acres permanently protected; cross-border pact links key habitats
item.description: A groundbreaking conservation project has successfully preserved 181 acres of forests and wetlands straddling Maryland and Delaware. Championed by the Porter family alongside multiple conservation entities, the Henry F. Porter Preserve focuses on safeguarding vital ecosystems. This initiative not only emphasizes sustainable practices but also plays a pivotal role in the overall protection of the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

item.title: Minnesota neighbours lose $148,500 award as court settles nine-year lake access dispute
item.description: A nine-year property dispute over access to Minnesota's Prairie Lake has taken another turn after an appeals court upheld a ruling in favour of the Blackwood Trust. The Monday decision confirms the trust's direct access to the lake and leaves an earlier $148,500 trespass award to neighbouring property owners cancelled. The dispute centred on conflicting land surveys dating back to 1997.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US midterms: FBI, ICE agents will not serve as election monitors, DOJ says
item.description: The US Department of Justice has decided that FBI personnel will not oversee polling sites during upcoming elections. Concerns were raised regarding potential intimidation of voters, especially from minority communities. Civil rights groups, led by the NAACP, filed a lawsuit to prevent federal law enforcement at polling places. Federal election monitors will be present but will not have law enforcement powers.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Michigan appeals court upholds $9.7 million verdict after mother dies following tummy tuck surgery
item.description: In a landmark decision, a Michigan court has affirmed a nearly $9.7 million ruling against Henry Ford Macomb Hospital for negligence that led to Cathleen Allen's tragic death after cosmetic surgery complications. Medical testimony highlighted that prompt action could have preserved her life. The jury attributed liability to both the surgeon and hospital, underscoring the urgent need for stringent patient safety measures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Gerard Butler visited Liberia in 2013; Mary’s Meals has delivered 260 million meals since 2006
item.description: Gerard Butler is a passionate advocate for Mary's Meals, an organization dedicated to providing vital school meals for children in Liberia. Since its launch in 2006, the charity has served over 260 million meals, making a meaningful difference in children's nutrition and education. Reaching more than 95,000 children daily through local volunteers, the program exemplifies community engagement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Summerhouse Use Under Review: Jason Statham seeks lawful status for guest annexe; 1973 rule under scrutiny
item.description: Jason Statham and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley are facing challenges in planning the summerhouse at their Hampshire estate. They have submitted a request for a certificate of lawfulness to transform the structure, initially approved as a swimming-pool pavilion, into residential quarters. Although the summerhouse has served as guest accommodation for prior owners since 2012, the New Forest National Park Authority is currently assessing the appropriateness of their application.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australian couple postpone wedding to build dream castle; 22 years later, it remains unfinished
item.description: An Australian couple who postponed their wedding to build a fairytale castle in Tasmania are still working on it 22 years later. Christina Kent and Francis Shepherd have used around 100,000 bricks to construct the 27-room Castle Phoenix, which stands 17 metres tall. Despite financial and health challenges, only three of its eight turrets are complete, and their wedding remains on hold.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US judge Alvin Hellerstein, who handled Maduro trial, dies at 92
item.description: Alvin K Hellerstein, a distinguished federal judge known for presiding over major cases, passed away Wednesday morning with his family by his side. He dedicated his judicial career to the US District Court for the Southern District of New York from 1998 and dealt with high-profile matters, including those of Nicolás Maduro and President Donald Trump's hush money.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Hegseth fires top Pentagon military planner as Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes: Report
item.description: Army Lt Gen Brett Sylvia has been removed from his post, raising concerns amid escalating tensions with Iran. President Donald Trump is reportedly considering military action against Iran after the midterm elections. Several regional governments are preparing for potential Iranian retaliation if hostilities resume, which may also affect energy infrastructure. Additionally, the military is increasing its presence in the Persian Gulf with new deployments.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Fuel costs jump from $1,800 to $8,000: Cruise ship residents forced ashore in Cambodia
item.description: Cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey had to disembark its passengers in Cambodia due to soaring fuel expenses. The ship had operated for over two years, accommodating long-term residents on board. As fuel costs increased significantly, the company announced the suspension of operations. Passengers were provided with temporary accommodation while some already departed for their destinations. The ship is expected to refuel before continuing its journey after leaving Cambodia.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey
